newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan says room for flexibility on infotech pact.
newsitem.headline: Japan says room for flexibility on infotech pact.

text.p: Gaps remain between the European Union (EU) and Japan on aspects of a proposed deal to scrap tariffs on information technology products by 2000, but there may be room for flexibility, a Japanese government source told reporters on Tuesday.
He was speaking after Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda met EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan for about an hour.

"We have not reached a compromise on non-tariff measures. On product coverage, we still haven't solved differences on sensitive items for quad members. There may be some flexibility -- I don't know," the source said.
He said Brittan and Ikeda did not discuss the issue of China's application to join the WTO, but added that Brittan wanted to bring up the issue at the working lunch.
He added that the main issues at the working lunch would be the information technology agreement and the telecommunications negotiations.
But the source also said the infotech deal would be a key focus of a working lunch among the Big Four ministers on Tuesday. The four are the EU, Japan, the United States and Canada.

He added that the ministers were unlikely to reach an agreement at the lunch, but might get close. "Without instructions from the ministers, it will be difficult to pull it together at the working level this afternoon," he said.
He also said that Brittan and Ikeda discussed efforts to reach a WTO agreement on telecoms services and that this issue seemed to moving towards resolution.
